bull.b: A predominantly recurring, long-term contract model can make revenue more predictable and deepen operator relationships. It also supports ongoing monetization of established content and platforms, providing a durable base for cash generation and reinvestment.

Substantial EBITDA margin expansion indicates improving operating economics despite tax increases. If retained, higher margins can strengthen cash generation, improve resilience against regulatory costs, and create greater flexibility to invest in content, platforms, and market expansion.

Share gains across key markets and a larger non-U.K. revenue base reduce reliance on any single geography and broaden the company's growth runway. Greater diversification can support more durable expansion as North America, Greece, and other markets become larger contributors.

bear.b: High debt combined with persistent negative equity materially limits financial flexibility. The capital structure can constrain investment and capital allocation, while requiring a meaningful portion of future cash generation to support debt obligations and preserve covenant headroom.

Recent top-line contraction and recurring net losses show that strong gross and EBITDA margins have not yet translated into stable earnings. Continued volatility could restrict internal funding, weaken confidence in forward profitability, and make growth investments harder to sustain.

The Brazil shutdown has delayed growth expectations and reduced guidance, while higher U.K. gaming taxes directly pressure earnings and free-cash-flow conversion. These regulatory changes can persist across several periods and require mitigation through product and geographic expansion.
